summary: Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche (circa 1870–1887) and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso (circa 1870–1912). He also taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (including president, 1963–1966), Keio University, and Komazawa University.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Florida, Florida State University, and the University of Virginia (PhD ~1991). She held teaching posts at Virginia, Indiana University Indianapolis, and Florida State University.
Tessa Verney Wheeler was an archaeology and history scholar. She studied at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He held professorships at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1972), and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1972–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, Leipzig, and Berlin. He was a professor and dean at the University of Tokyo, and later served as president of Daito Bunka University.

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Komazawa University. He held multiple academic posts, including president of Komazawa University (2002–2006) and president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuro Noguchi was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at Yokohama National University (~1968–1978), the University of Tsukuba (~1978–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2003).

Tetsuro Watsuji specialized in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and under Martin Heidegger and Natsume Sōseki, he held professorships in ethics at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo.

Tetsuzo Tanikawa was a philosopher who studied at the First Higher School and Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1925–1931) and served as a professor at Hosei University (~1938–1965).
Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held posts at Utrecht University, including committee member (attested 1989) and professor emeritus (attested 2000).
Thanissaro Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Oberlin College and trained under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko (~1976–1986). He co-founded Metta Forest Monastery and became its abbot in 1993.
Thanon Chitkament is a researcher in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under guides V. D. Gogte and P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Berlin. He held posts as privatdozent at Berlin, at the Bodleian Library, and as professor at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Bonn.

Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He spent his career there as privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and ordinarius professor (1862–1881).
Theodor Bloch was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch (~1888–1892) and later studied under Georg Bühler (~1892–1894).

Theodor Goldstücker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg and Bonn under Peter von Bohlen, Karl Rosenkranz, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He was professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1852 to 1872.

Theodor Nöldeke was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. Educated at Göttingen, Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin, he was a professor at the University of Kiel and later at the University of Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig and Göttingen under Georg Curtius, Hermann Brockhaus, Hermann Sauppe, and Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at the University of Greifswald and the University of Halle (1890–1921).
